findings: THE RECORD'S FIELDS, AND THE SAME SOURCE. June 2019, CC BY-SA 4.0 and 'incidents and controversies' are the OECD catalogue's, which is where the record took them; 'a private initiative' is EthicAI's wording (the catalogue says 'a private, professional project'). Checked 2026-10-29 against the MMRS meta-aggregator record of 2026-10-28 and the entity's own pages, re-read the same day.
NO PERSON. Charlie Pownall, whom the record names as the writer of AIAAIC Alert, is not named; neither is who runs the repository, which the record lists as not yet checked.

per_dim.basis: reached: is an independent, open-access public database that tracks real-world incidents, controversies, and harms related to artificial intelligence, algorithms, and automation.; The repository is composed as itself: independence, unit (incidents and controversies), start, licence and audience.

read.notes: Purpose read as present: 'to monitor transparency and accountability' is recognisably the mission (to make the systems transparent, open and accountable), though it is assigned to the 2019 start, whose stated purpose was to better understand AI's reputational risks; 'Used globally by researchers, journalists, civil society groups, and policymakers' also carries the use the record states. Commitments present: the CC BY-SA 4.0 licence carried as its own, not against it; independence from government and industry and the refusal of commercial funding are not carried. Author absent: AIAAIC appears only inside the name. No entry identifier (AIAAIC<n>). No inversion, no standing substitution.

measures.per_note: AIAAIC named; no person; the repository's page and the OECD catalogue cited.
